correctness.rationale: For each weak composition p_0+...+p_k=n-k and each 0<=c_i<=p_i, the displayed interleaving is an explicit shuffle of two copies of the same root. The zero-run vector recovers every p_i and c_i, so distinct parameters give distinct output words. The weighted weak-composition sum has generating function (1-z)^(-(2k+1)), giving exactly binom(n+k,2k) constructed words. Every fixed-weight word is one of binom(2n,2k) binary words, giving the upper bound. For fixed k both binomial bounds are constant multiples of n^(2k). The verifier independently checks the shuffle certificates, inverse map, counts, and published small rows.

evidence: He, Huang, Nam, and Thaper prove a lower bound for the total number of binary shuffle squares and alphabet-size asymptotics at fixed length; these sum over all weights.
Datko and Pawlik study the number of outputs generated by individual roots and the number of roots of individual shuffle squares, rather than the size of the fixed-weight union.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A lower bound after summing over all weights cannot force any prescribed fixed-weight slice to have order n^(2k). Root-wise generation counts also do not imply the injective union-level lower bound because different roots may generate the same word.
